source_evidence.anchor: section 1 opening QR and Householder definitions
source_evidence.observation: The paper defines QR for A in R^(m x n) with m >= n, exact orthogonal Q in R^(m x m), and upper-trapezoidal R in R^(m x n). A Householder matrix has the form P = I - 2vv^T/(v^Tv), with v nonzero, and Householder QR applies P_n ... P_1 A = R with Q = (P_n ... P_1)^T.

source_evidence.anchor: norm, column, and constant conventions following equation (1.1)
source_evidence.observation: The vector norm is ||x||_2 = (x^Tx)^(1/2), the matrix 2-norm is its subordinate norm, ||A||_F = trace(A^TA)^(1/2), a_j denotes column j of A, and c_0,c_1,... are integer constants of modest size.
Each elementary floating-point operation is modeled by fl(x op y) = (x op y)(1 + delta), with |delta| <= u, where u is the unit roundoff.

For lambda > 0, gamma_tilde_k(lambda) is exp((lambda*sqrt(k)*u + k*u^2)/(1-u)) - 1 = lambda*sqrt(k)*u + O(u^2). Mean independence means E(delta_j | delta_(j-1),...,delta_1) = E(delta_j) in generation order.

source_evidence.anchor: Model 1.5 and its following applicability paragraph
source_evidence.observation: Model 1.5 assumes that rounding errors generated in computation order satisfy (1.4), are mean independent, and have mean zero. The paper notes that round-to-nearest errors need not satisfy this model in every computation, while stochastic-rounding errors do.

The Householder-vector construction is analyzed probabilistically; after normalizing the representation to P = I - vv^T with ||v||_2 = sqrt(2), the computed vector is v_hat = v + Delta v with a componentwise bound involving c_4 gamma_tilde_k(lambda) + O(u^2).

For given P_j = I - v_jv_j^T with v_j^Tv_j = 2, vector application is computed as b_(j+1) = b_j - (v_j^Tb_j)v_j. The result has the perturbed-product form b_hat_(r+1) = (P_r + Delta P_r)...(P_1 + Delta P_1)b, and ||Delta P_j||_2 <= c_5 gamma_tilde_m(lambda) simultaneously for all j with probability at least 1 - 2rm exp(-lambda^2/2).

The remaining section results replace the probabilistic local result by the stronger assumption that (4.2) holds with probability 1 for every j. Under that assumption, Lemma 4.2 gives ||Delta b||_2 <= c_6 lambda sqrt(r) gamma_tilde_m(lambda)||b||_2 + O(u^2) with probability at least 1 - 2m exp(-lambda^2).
The matrix-concentration step bounds the accumulated first-order perturbation in operator 2-norm and yields the vector backward error Delta b = Eb + O(u^2), retaining an additive O(u^2) term.

Applying the vector result to all n columns gives a simultaneous columnwise matrix backward-error bound, with probability at least 1 - 2mn exp(-lambda^2), by bounding the probability of failure in at least one column.

For the computed upper-trapezoidal Householder QR factor R_hat, under Model 1.5 and Lemma 4.2's assumption, there is an exact orthogonal Q such that A + Delta A = Q R_hat. Simultaneously for j = 1:n, ||Delta a_j||_2 <= c_6 lambda sqrt(n) gamma_tilde_m(lambda)||a_j||_2 + O(u^2), with probability at least 1 - 2mn exp(-lambda^2).

In the QR specialization, entries annihilated by a reflector are explicitly set to zero. The Householder vectors depend on previous computed quantities and are themselves computed; the proof says their construction errors add only an O(u^2) perturbation and do not alter the displayed first-order term.

The theorem is a first-order bound. The omitted second-order contribution has order mn^2u^2 relative to the input scale, versus first-order sqrt(mn)u dependence. The paper therefore requires m^(1/2)n^(3/2)u < 1 for the analysis to imply sqrt(mn)u growth; this is a post-theorem interpretation, contrasted with the worst-case condition mnu < 1.

source_evidence.anchor: paragraph beginning with removal of the Lemma 4.2 assumption
source_evidence.observation: The authors explicitly identify the probability-one local-bound assumption as an assumption they would ideally remove: it replaces the derived local probability 1 - 2rm exp(-lambda^2/2) by probability 1 because the required concentration theorem for probabilistic local bounds is unavailable.

The simultaneous columnwise bound implies ||Delta A||_F <= c_6 lambda sqrt(n) gamma_tilde_m(lambda)||A||_F + O(u^2). The paper summarizes the leading dimension dependence as reducing from mnu in the worst-case bound to sqrt(mn)u in the probabilistic bound.

binders: m and n are matrix dimensions, and A is a real m-by-n input matrix; the standing QR setup has m >= n. [PDF p. 1 (printed 1146), anchor: section 1 opening QR definition]
u is the unit roundoff appearing in the relative-error model. [PDF p. 2 (printed 1147), anchor: equation (1.4)]
lambda is a fixed positive probabilistic parameter. [PDF p. 2 (printed 1147), anchor: equation (1.6)]
delta_1,delta_2,... are the rounding errors ordered by their generation during the computation. [PDF p. 3 (printed 1148), anchor: Model 1.5]

R_hat in R^(m x n) is the computed upper-trapezoidal factor returned by Householder QR, and a_j is column j of the exact input A. [PDF p. 9 (printed 1154), anchor: Theorem 4.4; PDF p. 2 (printed 1147), anchor: column convention]
Q in R^(m x m) and Delta A in R^(m x n) are existential backward-error witnesses; Q is exactly orthogonal. [PDF p. 9 (printed 1154), anchor: equation (4.16)]
hypotheses: R_hat is obtained from A by the Householder QR algorithm, not by an arbitrary factorization procedure. [PDF p. 9 (printed 1154), anchor: Theorem 4.4]
Every elementary operation used by the computation satisfies fl(x op y) = (x op y)(1 + delta), |delta| <= u. [PDF p. 2 (printed 1147), anchor: equation (1.4)]
The generated rounding errors are mean independent in computation order and each has mean zero. [PDF p. 2 (printed 1147), anchor: Definition 1.3; PDF p. 3 (printed 1148), anchor: Model 1.5]

The local perturbed-reflector bound ||Delta P_j||_2 <= c_5 gamma_tilde_m(lambda) is assumed to hold with probability 1 for every reflector j, as required by Lemma 4.2. [PDF p. 7 (printed 1152), anchor: paragraph preceding Lemma 4.2 and Lemma 4.2]

For the tall QR setting, m >= n is inherited from the paper's standing definition even though Theorem 4.4 does not repeat it parenthetically. [PDF p. 1 (printed 1146), anchor: section 1 QR definition; PDF p. 10 (printed 1155), anchor: sentence following equation (4.19)]
conclusions: There exists an exact orthogonal Q such that the computed R_hat obeys the exact backward relation A + Delta A = Q R_hat. [PDF p. 9 (printed 1154), anchor: Theorem 4.4 and equation (4.16)]
For every j = 1,...,n, ||Delta a_j||_2 <= c_6 lambda sqrt(n) gamma_tilde_m(lambda)||a_j||_2 + O(u^2). [PDF p. 9 (printed 1154), anchor: equation (4.17)]

The column bounds are simultaneous and hold with probability at least p_4(lambda,m,n) = 1 - 2mn exp(-lambda^2), rather than with a separate probability guarantee for each column. [PDF p. 9 (printed 1154), anchor: Lemma 4.3 probability argument and Theorem 4.4]

The column bounds imply the Frobenius backward-error consequence ||Delta A||_F <= c_6 lambda sqrt(n) gamma_tilde_m(lambda)||A||_F + O(u^2). [PDF p. 10 (printed 1155), anchor: implication sentence and equation (4.20)]

Using gamma_tilde_m(lambda) = lambda sqrt(m)u + O(u^2), the displayed first-order factor has sqrt(mn)u dimension dependence, with constants and lambda factors retained in the exact displayed bound. [PDF p. 2 (printed 1147), anchor: equation (1.6); PDF p. 10 (printed 1155), anchor: conclusion following equation (4.20)]
definitions_and_conventions: gamma_tilde_k(lambda) = exp((lambda*sqrt(k)*u + k*u^2)/(1-u)) - 1 = lambda*sqrt(k)*u + O(u^2), with lambda > 0; the theorem uses k = m. [PDF p. 2 (printed 1147), anchor: equation (1.6); PDF p. 9 (printed 1154), anchor: equation (4.17)]

Mean independence is weaker than full independence: E(delta_j | delta_(j-1),...,delta_1) = E(delta_j), and Model 1.5 additionally sets E(delta_j) = 0. [PDF p. 2 (printed 1147), anchor: Definition 1.3; PDF p. 3 (printed 1148), anchor: Model 1.5]

The paper denotes column j of A by a_j and uses the same notation Delta a_j for column j of Delta A. [PDF p. 2 (printed 1147), anchor: column convention; PDF p. 9 (printed 1154), anchor: equation (4.17)]

A Householder matrix is exactly orthogonal and is represented in section 4 as P_j = I - v_jv_j^T with v_j^Tv_j = 2. [PDF p. 1 (printed 1146), anchor: Householder definition; PDF p. 6 (printed 1151), anchor: Lemma 4.1]
The constants c_0,c_1,..., including c_5 and c_6, are integer constants of modest size; no numerical value for c_6 is supplied. [PDF p. 2 (printed 1147), anchor: constant convention]
implicit_context: Theorem 4.4 specializes the r-reflector result to Householder QR with r = n, which accounts for sqrt(n) in (4.17). [PDF p. 1 (printed 1146), anchor: P_n ... P_1 A = R; PDF p. 9 (printed 1154), anchor: equation (4.17)]

Q is an exact orthogonal witness associated with the reflector product; it is not a computed Q_hat and no loss-of-orthogonality claim is part of Theorem 4.4. [PDF p. 9 (printed 1154), anchor: equation (4.16); PDF p. 10 (printed 1155), anchor: transition to Theorem 4.5]
The probability 1 - 2mn exp(-lambda^2) comes from making the columnwise result simultaneous through a failure-probability union bound. [PDF p. 9 (printed 1154), anchor: proof of Lemma 4.3]

The probability-one local bound is additional to Model 1.5 and is stronger than the local probability actually derived in Lemma 4.1. [PDF p. 6 (printed 1151), anchor: equation (4.2); PDF p. 7 (printed 1152), anchor: paragraph preceding Lemma 4.2]

statement.algorithm_linkage: The contract concerns the standard Householder QR reduction P_n ... P_1 A = R. Each reflector application is evaluated as b_(j+1) = b_j - (v_j^Tb_j)v_j and represented as multiplication by P_j + Delta P_j. In the QR specialization the active Householder vectors are computed from prior computed data, and entries intended to be annihilated are explicitly assigned zero; the proof accounts for vector-construction error as O(u^2). [PDF p. 1 (printed 1146), anchor: Householder QR construction; PDF p. 6 (printed 1151), anchor: Lemma 4.1 and equations (4.1)-(4.2); PDF p. 9 (printed 1154), anchor: proof of Theorem 4.4]
numerical_model: Relative-error model: fl(x op y) = (x op y)(1 + delta), |delta| <= u. [PDF p. 2 (printed 1147), anchor: equation (1.4)]

Probabilistic model: errors are indexed in actual computation order, are mean independent, and have zero mean; identical distributions and full mutual independence are not assumed. [PDF p. 2 (printed 1147), anchor: Definition 1.3; PDF p. 3 (printed 1148), anchor: Model 1.5]

The theorem additionally assumes the local operator-norm bound almost surely, although Lemma 4.1 derives it only with probability at least 1 - 2rm exp(-lambda^2/2). [PDF p. 6 (printed 1151), anchor: equation (4.2); PDF p. 7 (printed 1152), anchor: Lemma 4.2 assumption]

The paper treats lambda as a positive constant and gives the final event probability explicitly as 1 - 2mn exp(-lambda^2). [PDF p. 2 (printed 1147), anchor: equation (1.6); PDF p. 9 (printed 1154), anchor: Theorem 4.4]

The theorem is conditional on Model 1.5; the paper warns that round-to-nearest errors can violate mean independence or zero mean in some computations. [PDF p. 3 (printed 1148), anchor: paragraph following Model 1.5]
error_notions: Delta A is a backward perturbation of the exact input A because the computed R_hat is an exact QR factor of A + Delta A with an exact orthogonal Q. [PDF p. 9 (printed 1154), anchor: equation (4.16)]

Equation (4.17) is columnwise relative backward error: each perturbation column is compared with the corresponding exact input column in vector 2-norm. [PDF p. 9 (printed 1154), anchor: equation (4.17)]
Equation (4.20) is normwise Frobenius backward error and is a consequence of the simultaneous columnwise result. [PDF p. 10 (printed 1155), anchor: implication sentence and equation (4.20)]

contract_plain_english: Fix lambda > 0 and a real m-by-n matrix A in the paper's tall-matrix setting m >= n. Run Householder QR under the relative-error model with computation-order mean-independent, zero-mean rounding errors, and additionally assume that every local perturbed-reflector bound holds with probability 1. Then the computed upper-trapezoidal R_hat is the exact R factor of A + Delta A for some exact orthogonal Q. With probability at least 1 - 2mn exp(-lambda^2), all columns simultaneously satisfy ||Delta a_j||_2 <= c_6 lambda sqrt(n) gamma_tilde_m(lambda)||a_j||_2 + O(u^2), and consequently ||Delta A||_F <= c_6 lambda sqrt(n) gamma_tilde_m(lambda)||A||_F + O(u^2). Here gamma_tilde_m(lambda) has the exact exponential definition in (1.6), with first-order expansion lambda sqrt(m)u + O(u^2). The omitted terms must be retained, and m^(1/2)n^(3/2)u < 1 is only the paper's subsequent condition for regarding the sqrt(mn)u first-order rate as dominant.
